observations:
Torah #213 is a compact, tightly unified teaching that resolves cleanly into exactly two packages — one good and one evil — with no residual concepts requiring additional packages.

The Torah's entire conceptual vocabulary falls into two domains:

  Package 1 (GOOD) — שֵׁם סָאל וְהַהַסְתָּרָה: The Divine Name SAL (formed from the acrostic of Psalm 32:7), the concealment/covering it provides, the verse 'אַתָּה סֵתֶר לִי,' and the verse 'מִצַּר תִּצְּרֵנִי וּתְשַׁמְּרֵנִי' (in its protective valence). These are all expressions of the same protective reality.

  Package 2 (EVIL) — סָמֶ"ךְ-מֵ"ם וְאוֹת מֵ"ם: Samael, the Accuser (בַּעַל דָּבָר), the letter Mem in all its evil manifestations (Mem of death, Mem of 'mitzar'), and the doom-acrostic 'סוֹף אָדָם לָמוּת' (when Samael has gained power). These are all expressions of the same destructive circling force.

Candidates examined and rejected for independent package status:

1. THE LETTER-COMBINATION DOMAIN (צֵרוּף, אוֹתִיּוֹת, נוֹטָרִיקוֹן): Torah #213 operates through the mechanism of letter-combination (the Name SAL = ס-א-ל as acrostic; Samael = SAL + Mem). One might wonder if letters/combinations constitute a third, neutral package. But in this Torah, letters are not an independent domain — they are entirely instrumentalized: the Mem is ONLY discussed as a bechina of Samael (evil package), and the acrostic letters are ONLY discussed as the Name SAL (good package). There is no neutral letter-domain here the way there is in, e.g., Torah #1 (where אות ח"י"ת and אות נו"ן and אות ו"א"ו are independent structural packages). Rejected.

2. THE VERSE PSALM 32:7 AS A DOMAIN: One might consider making 'Psalm 32:7' or 'the verse' its own neutral package (since the verse contains both the protective acrostic AND the dangerous Mem). However, the verse is not discussed as an entity with its own domain — its two halves are assigned to their respective packages (the first half to the good package, the Mem of the second half to the evil package). The verse is a structural vehicle, not an independent thematic cluster. Rejected.

3. THE DEATH/DOOM DOMAIN (מָוֶת, גְּזֵרָה, death-decree): Death is mentioned as what the Name protects from (line 1) and recurs in 'מֵ"ם שֶׁל מָוֶת' and 'סוֹף אָדָם לָמוּת.' But there is no separate death-package — death and doom are entirely subsumed within the evil Samael cluster. Samael IS death; the Mem of death IS Samael. Three or more nodes with independent bechina connections outside the existing packages are required to warrant a new package; the death-domain has no such independent cluster. Rejected.

Conclusion: The good/evil mirror structure in Torah #213 is unusually clean and binary. The same three letters (ס-א-ל) constitute either divine protection (Package 1) or doom (Package 2 — 'סוֹף אָדָם לָמוּת') depending on whether the Mem of the Accuser has breached the protective covering. This is a complete and self-contained two-package architecture with a single eitza bridge (the practical instruction to pause when reciting the verse) flowing between them.
